The waiting period for pre-existing diseases is 36 months on standard retail plans, unless explicitly waived in writing by Aurora on the policy schedule [3][5]. For the Aurora Senior Care plan (ages 60 and above), the waiting period for pre-existing diseases is reduced to 24 months [5].
The grace period for an annual policy is 30 days from the renewal due date [1][5].
As of 1 April 2026, Aurora's network covers 11,400 hospitals across 780 towns [1].

The no-claim bonus on the Aurora Gold plan is 25% of the base sum insured per claim-free year, accumulating up to a maximum of 100% [1][5]. If a claim is made, the bonus is not reduced, but stops accumulating for that year only [1].

If you are not satisfied with the initial outcome, you can escalate the matter to Aurora's Grievance Redressal Officer (GRO) [2]. If Aurora's final response remains unsatisfactory, you may approach the Insurance Ombudsman for your region [1].

All plans include road ambulance cover of ₹5,000 per hospitalisation [1]. Additionally, the Aurora Gold plan provides air ambulance cover of up to ₹2,50,000 per policy year within India on prior authorisation [5].

Yes, in-patient treatment for mental illness is covered on the same terms as physical illness, as required by the Mental Healthcare Act 2017 [1]. The standard 30-day initial waiting period applies, but there is no separate waiting period for it [1].

The free-look period is the window in which a new policy can be returned for a refund [3]. A policyholder may cancel within 15 days of receiving the policy document, or 30 days if the policy was sold through distance marketing [1][2]. Upon cancellation within this window, the premium is refunded minus the proportionate risk premium for the period of cover, medical examination costs, and stamp duty [2].
You earn 150 wellness points per year for completing an annual health check-up [1].

A day-care procedure is a procedure requiring less than 24 hours of hospitalisation due to technological advances, making it payable despite the general 24-hour admission requirement [3]. Out-patient treatment is not considered a day-care procedure [3].
For an emergency admission under the cashless route, the hospital must notify Aurora within 24 hours of admission [1][5].

Dependent parents can be added to Silver (at an extra premium), Gold, and Platinum plans, but are not allowed on the Bronze plan [1]. When a parent is added, the overall policy premium is determined by the age of the eldest member covered, which often costs more than an individual senior-citizen policy for that parent [4].

Credit for the waiting periods you have already served will carry over, but only up to the sum insured of your previous policy (including any accrued no-claim bonus) [1][2]. Any increase or excess in the sum insured will be subject to fresh waiting periods on that incremental amount [1][2].

To continue your baby's coverage beyond the initial 90 days, you must inform Aurora and add the newborn to the policy as a dependent within 90 days of birth [1]. If requested within this 90-day window, adding the newborn is guaranteed-issue with no medical underwriting, whereas requests made afterward will treat the child as a fresh applicant [1]. If you need to submit a reimbursement claim for the hospitalisation, it must be submitted within 30 days of discharge [3].

A claim on the Aurora Silver plan reduces your accumulated no-claim bonus by 10 percentage points [1]. It does not reset the accumulated bonus to zero [1].
Under the Gold plan, the coverage limit for a Caesarean section is ₹1,00,000 per delivery [1]. If the hospital bills ₹1,60,000, the out-of-pocket cost would be ₹60,000 [1].

Knee joint replacement is generally not covered immediately, as it is subject to a 24-month waiting period [1][5]. However, if the knee replacement is required following an accidental injury, it is covered immediately from day one [1][2][5].

Total discounts are capped at 30% of the base premium [1]. However, the wellness discount (which can be up to 15%) is applied last, after the cap, and is the only discount permitted to exceed the 30% limit [1][3][5].

Cashless access will be denied if the hospital is an excluded provider [2][3]. Your only option is to file for reimbursement, which is payable only if the admission was a genuine emergency, no alternative facility was reachable, and pre-approval is obtained [1][3][5].

The deadline depends on the claim type: you have 45 days from the date of the query to respond for reimbursement claims [5], and failing to respond within 45 days results in Aurora closing the claim [2]. However, for motor insurance claims, the deadline to respond to a query is 30 days from the date of the query [4].

The sources disagree on the notification timeline. According to one source, planned cashless admission must be notified 48 hours before admission [1], while other sources state that it must be notified at least 72 hours before admission [2][3].

Aurora settles or rejects a reimbursement claim within 15 working days of receiving the last required document [1][2]. If Aurora raises a query, the timeline restarts once the requested document is supplied [1]. Under archived 2024 rules, the settlement timeline was 30 days from the last document [3].
The Aurora Gold plan has no co-payment at all ages [1]. The Aurora Silver plan also has no co-payment for claims where the eldest insured member is below 60 years of age [2].

Across the four plans, pre-hospitalisation cover is provided for 30 days, 45 days, 60 days, and 90 days, respectively [1]. Post-hospitalisation cover across the four plans is 60 days, 90 days, 120 days, and 180 days, respectively [1].

You should choose the Gold plan (or Platinum plan), as dependent parents-in-law are eligible for coverage under Gold and Platinum tiers [1]. Furthermore, the Gold plan removes room-rent sub-limits [3].

Out-patient dental work is not covered under any plan [1]. Furthermore, dental treatment and oral surgery are permanently excluded across all Aurora indemnity plans, unless necessitated by an accidental injury that requires hospitalisation [2][3].
